title.value: Genomic epidemiology and associated clinical outcomes of a SARS-CoV-2 outbreak in a general adult hospital in Quebec
title.justification: The title extracted reflects the study in the research paper, focusing on the SARS-CoV-2 outbreak and its genomic epidemiology carried out in Quebec.
title.quote: Genomic epidemiology and associated clinical outcomes of a SARS-CoV-2 outbreak in a general adult hospital in Quebec

analysis.description: The paper discusses the genomic epidemiology of a SARS-CoV-2 outbreak in Quebec, Canada. It uses whole genome nanopore sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs from positive cases in two hospitals to assess viral diversity. The paper identifies multiple subclades and clinical features associated with them.

type.justification: The study involves practical data collection and analysis of SARS-CoV-2 genomic sequences and clinical features associated with a specific outbreak.
type.quote: Here, we describe the use of tiled amplicon, whole genome nanopore sequencing to resolve the genomic diversity of 242 SARS-CoV-2 infections in this local outbreak and to rapidly disseminate the sequences to the international community.

name.justification: The research mainly revolves around the genomic sequencing and analysis of SARS-CoV-2 strains during an outbreak.
name.quote: We performed tiled amplicon whole genome nanopore sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs from all SARS-CoV-2 positive samples from 31 March to 17 April 2020 in 2 local hospitals to assess the viral diversity of the outbreak.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 by discussing transmission patterns, viral diversity, and clinical outcomes related to the viral strains.
name.quote: To validate if the abundance of a particular subclade was due to hospital-acquired transmission or if the observed lineage frequencies were representative of SARS-CoV-2 lineages in the local community, we compared the distribution of viral genotypes between 2 different hospitals.

name.justification: The study incorporates the analysis of clinical data correlating symptoms and patient outcomes with the genomic data from the virus.
name.quote: We associate viral genomes with clinical features, including symptoms and mortality, and present longitudinal sequencing data from 21 infected individuals.

name.justification: Medaka is used as a neural network for the experimental version of the ARTIC Network bioinformatics pipeline for genome consensus production.
name.quote: The experimental version, which uses the Medaka neural network and Longshot variant caller.

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses Medaka as an existing tool for consensus production rather than introducing it as a novel contribution.
is_contributed.quote: We assessed the impact of two different versions of the ARTIC Network bioinformatics pipeline on consensus genome production: (i) The default version using signal-level correction with Nanopolish and (ii) the experimental version, which uses the Medaka neural network.

is_executed.justification: Medaka is actively used in the experimental pipeline of the study for genome sequencing data analysis.
is_executed.quote: The experimental version, which uses the Medaka neural network and Longshot variant caller.

is_compared.justification: Medaka is compared to another model (Nanopolish) to assess its efficiency in genome consensus generation.
is_compared.quote: Excluding regions covered by less than 20 reads, the Nanopolish version generated an average of 2.9 ± 3.5 (standard deviation) ambiguous bases ('N') per genome, versus 1.1 ± 2.5 for Medaka.
